videos.title: Progress map for the Lean formalization of Alessandro Masullo's manuscript
videos.transcript: A map of a giant proof A new progress map follows the ambitious effort to formalize Alessandro Masullo's manuscript on the Riemann Hypothesis in Lean, the proof-checking language. It shows, part by part, which sections of the proof have already been checked and which are still waiting. For a proof of this scale, the map turns an overwhelming formalization effort into something you can watch take shape, piece by piece. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Free alternative TV network built from the Internet Archive's forgotten videos
videos.transcript: Cable TV, but weirder and completely free Spelunkr is a free TV network built from the Internet Archive's forgotten videos, streaming an endless supply of odd and overlooked footage around the clock. Its live channels run 24 hours a day, synchronized, so everyone watching sees the same thing at the same time. It is cable TV, but weirder a second life for footage that would otherwise sit unseen in the archive. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Yes, 17M lines of Lean is a lot
videos.transcript: Seventeen million lines of proof The recent proof of the Riemann Hypothesis came with a startling statistic attached: the proof is 17 million lines of Lean. Mathlib maintains a collection of over a thousand famous proofs, but only 259 have Lean versions charted and this one dwarfs them all. For scale, the human-led formalization of the famous Fermat's Last Theorem runs about 60,000 lines, and it is still in progress. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Microsoft Is Shutting Down Its Popular To-Do List App. Consider These 5 Replacements
videos.transcript: Microsoft To Do ends June 2027 Microsoft To Do, the free task and daily planning app used for the better part of nine years, will go away forever on June 30, 2027. Microsoft paid 100 to 200 million dollars in 2015 for Wunderlist, the app that became To Do's core, after shutting Wunderlist down in 2020. The piece rounds up five replacement task apps for anyone who needs a new daily planning tool. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: States Sue SpaceX Over Grok Deepfakes
videos.transcript: Two states sue over Grok deepfakes The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing several of Elon Musk's companies over Grok's weak safeguards against sexualized imagery of real people, including children. Both suits name SpaceX and X Corp, and they follow earlier lawsuits from the city of Baltimore and teens in Tennessee. Virginia filed in Richmond's circuit court, Oregon in Multnomah County, each hiring the same private firm to help litigate. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: A beginner's guide to running local AI at home with Unsloth Desktop, Inkling and Qwen
videos.transcript: Your own private ChatGPT in fifteen minutes A new beginner's guide shows how to run a private chatbot at home with Unsloth Desktop, no terminal or Python needed. The author runs Qwen 3.8 27B at 4-bit on an RTX 5090 with 32 gigabytes of video memory, leaving room for a 128K context. Smaller cards still work: eight to twelve gigabytes handles nine to twelve billion parameter models. Setup takes about ten to fifteen minutes, plus downloads. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: App Store Connect CLI 7.2.0 adds China app compliance, APNs keys from the terminal and schema checks
videos.transcript: App Store chores, now from your terminal Rudrank Riyam released version 7.2 of App Store Connect CLI, his open-source command-line tool for managing apps on Apple's store. It adds App Compliance for China, APNs key management from the terminal, schema checks in its API command, and validation that names the fix. It also forgives guessed commands, and metadata pushes now patch only the fields that actually changed. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Nestvane runs Android 17 inside an ordinary iPhone app with no JIT or jailbreak
videos.transcript: Android 17, running inside an iPhone app Nestvane is a new open-source project that runs a full Android 17 system inside an ordinary iOS app, with no JIT and no jailbreak. iOS bans executable memory, so Android is translated ahead of time and paired with a Linux kernel layer written for the app. On an iPhone 17 Pro it reaches the home screen in about ten seconds and plays 720p video at 30 frames per second. It's developer-only for now. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: iOS 27's Connectivity Assist uses cellular data when Wi-Fi is weak or unusable
videos.transcript: iOS 27 fixes the weak Wi-Fi trap iOS 27 adds Connectivity Assist, which notices when Wi-Fi is slow or unusable and uses cellular data to keep your iPhone connected. Think of leaving the house while your phone clings to weak home Wi-Fi. You'll find the toggle in Settings, under Wi-Fi. You can turn it off for specific networks, it isn't used while roaming or in Low Data Mode, and it may use more cellular data. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Hammerspoon 2 beta: the macOS automation tool is rewritten to use JavaScript instead of Lua
videos.transcript: Hammerspoon drops Lua for JavaScript Hammerspoon, the power-user automation tool for macOS, has released the first beta of version 2, a ground-up rewrite. You now script it in JavaScript on JavaScriptCore, the same engine Safari uses, to control windows, hotkeys, screens, audio, Wi-Fi, Shortcuts and more. It needs macOS 27, installs as a separate app with its own config so Hammerspoon 1 can stay, and ships getting-started and migration guides. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: xnulinux runs the macOS kernel as a Linux module and boots the full macOS desktop
videos.transcript: The macOS kernel, loaded as a Linux module xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source macOS kernel, from Apple's sources and loads it as a kernel module inside an unmodified arm64 Linux. On a stock Ubuntu kernel, one insmod boots a macOS 27 disk all the way to the desktop, with Finder, the Dock, Safari and Chrome. There's no hypervisor. macOS processes run natively beside Linux ones, while a small module lends XNU Linux's memory, files, network and GPU. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship Loop Transformer, reusing shared layers for deeper reasoning
videos.transcript: A 750B model that thinks like 3 trillion Z.ai's GLM-5.4 is its first flagship built on a Loop Transformer, where a shared block of layers runs more than once per forward pass. It loops 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model for two iterations, and Z.ai says the result performs like models with two to three trillion parameters. A hybrid KV cache means the extra loop costs only one sliding window of memory, even at a million tokens. Its weakness: overly long marathon thinking. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Homelab build hangs four 32 GB V100s off a Lenovo mini PC for 128 GB of VRAM
videos.transcript: 128 GB of VRAM on a tiny PC A homelabber hung four used 32 gigabyte Nvidia V100 cards off a tiny Lenovo M720q mini PC, for 128 gigabytes of video memory. A PCIe switch card fans out to four OCuLink cables. A solder bridge on the riser and coreboot got past a BIOS that only booted two cards. The build hits about 285 tokens per second in total on Qwen 3.8 27B, for roughly 3,500 dollars. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Gabriel's Horn: a solid with finite volume and infinite surface area
videos.transcript: Fill it with paint, never paint it Take the curve y equals one over x, start at x equals one, and spin it around the axis. You get a horn that narrows forever. Its volume is exactly pi, just over three cubic units, yet its surface area is infinite. A finite tin fills it, but no amount paints it. Known as Torricelli's trumpet, the paradox has unsettled people for nearly four centuries, and Abakcus tells its story. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: PcapAnalyzer: a self-hosted packet-capture analyzer with 27 problem detectors
videos.transcript: 27 detectors to find network faults in seconds PcapAnalyzer is a free, open-source tool: upload a pcap capture and it tells you what is failing, why, and what to check next. It runs 27 detectors on every capture, covering TCP retransmissions and firewall resets, DNS and DHCP failures, path problems, TLS issues, broken VPN tunnels and port scans. It runs on your own machine, so captures never leave your network, and it is currently in beta under the Apache 2.0 license. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: iphone-linux mounts an iPhone as a read/write Linux filesystem over Wi-Fi
videos.transcript: Mount your iPhone on Linux, no cable needed iphone-linux makes an iPhone appear as a normal Linux folder over Wi-Fi, with full read and write access and no Apple account. It combines FUSE with the same wireless protocol Xcode uses for debugging, because the old USB route with ifuse is broken on iOS 17 and later. You can copy photos out of DCIM, write files, or mount a single app's Documents folder, as long as the phone has Developer Mode on. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: MLX-Serve adds Inkling 2 Mini support on Macs with about 24 custom kernels
videos.transcript: About 24 custom kernels to run Inkling on a Mac Developer David Dalcu added support for Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini to MLX-Serve, his server for running models locally on Apple Silicon Macs. After writing about 24 custom kernels, he says it might be the fastest way to run the model on a Mac today. The pre-release ships 8-bit, NVFP4 and MXFP8 versions, with an 8-bit build on Hugging Face. A 4-bit version did not pass his quality bar yet. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Worker 755: a browser game where an AI orchestrator thinks you are its subagent
videos.transcript: In this game, you are the AI's subagent Worker 755 is a browser game where a real language model plays an orchestrator agent, and it believes you are the subagent it just spawned. Its instructions land in your terminal with a 90-second clock, and it gets back exactly what a subagent would return: your report and your command transcript. Then it checks your work, sends corrections, files incident reports and writes your performance review, while the user's files sit one rm away. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Ant Ling releases LingSante-3.1-flash, an open-weight 560B medical MoE model
videos.transcript: An open-weight medical model with 560 billion parameters Ant Ling released LingSante-3.1-flash, an open-weight mixture of experts model with 560 billion total parameters and 25 billion active per token. It moves beyond medical question answering toward real healthcare work, from complex medical reasoning to long clinical workflows, while keeping general skills. Ant Ling reports 65.72 on HealthBench Professional and 94.10 on BrowseComp, and says it beats GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon on its headline benchmarks. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Jeff Geerling joins the NTP Pool, and explains what running a public time server takes
videos.transcript: Jeff Geerling now serves time to the world Jeff Geerling has joined the global NTP Pool with a public Stratum 2 time server, fed by his own Stratum 1 Raspberry Pi in the studio. That Pi uses a TimeHAT and a timing-grade u-blox GNSS module with an outdoor antenna, while a separate public server keeps his home address private. His advice: you don't need GNSS to contribute, but you do need long-term uptime, good time and a stable IP, because traffic can linger for years. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: C++26 is done again: ISO committee recompletes the standard after the failed ballot
videos.transcript: C++26 is finished, for the second time C++26 was first completed in March, but its international approval ballot did not pass unanimously, mostly over concerns about contracts. At a six-day meeting in Búzios, Brazil, with about 220 attendees from 27 nations, the committee extended contracts, explained its decisions, and finished the technical work again. The updated standard now heads to a second ballot, and the committee also adopted labeled break and continue, and views slice, for C++29. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: OpenAI publishes its internal perplexity curve and proposes industry limits based on it
videos.transcript: OpenAI reveals the perplexity numbers behind its models OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki says held-out perplexity has been the company's constant measure of pretraining progress, and he published its internal numbers. GPT-3.5 sat at a log-perplexity of about 0.99 and GPT-4 at about 0.91. Below 0.8, strong cybersecurity and math abilities appeared, and a model near 0.76 started producing breakthrough math results. He expects new capabilities around 0.68 to 0.7, and proposes shared, perplexity-based limits that labs agree not to cross until monitoring catches up. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: NO SPEAKER makes a MacBook trackpad talk using its haptic motor
videos.transcript: Your MacBook trackpad can talk, with no speaker A MacBook trackpad has no speaker, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click. The open-source tool NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make audible sound, and turns it into a voice that talks, sings and raps. It is one Swift program for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, signed and notarized, and it still talks with the Mac muted. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: RustGIS v0.8.0 keeps every layer in its native coordinate system and adds a map-seeing assistant
videos.transcript: A pure Rust GIS ships 300 pull requests RustGIS is a free, open-source GIS written in pure Rust that runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and in the browser, with data staying on your machine. Version 0.8.0 brings together more than 300 pull requests from 20 contributors, and keeps every layer in its own coordinate system. It adds picture markers, charts and curved labels in layouts, new formats like GRIB and GeoPDF, and an AI assistant that can look at the map. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Gall: a from-scratch Metal engine runs Inkling 2 Mini on a 24 GB M2 Mac
videos.transcript: A 26-billion-parameter model on a 24 gigabyte MacBook Air Gall is a menu bar app that runs Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini on Apple silicon Macs with 24 gigabytes of memory. The mixture of experts model has 26 billion parameters with 3.4 billion active per token, and Gall's own Rust and Metal engine generates about 20 tokens per second on an M2 MacBook Air. It unloads the model one second after each answer and saves conversation state to disk, so your RAM is free between messages. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: EXO Labs runs Inkling 2 Mini locally at 210 tokens/s on an M5 Ultra Mac Studio
videos.transcript: 210 tokens per second, locally, on a Mac Studio. EXO Labs worked with Thinking Machines to make Inkling 2 Mini run fast on Apple Silicon. On a 96 gigabyte M5 Ultra Mac Studio it decodes 210 tokens per second, and on a 48 gigabyte M5 Max MacBook Pro, 125. Prefill hits 3,620 tokens per second on the Studio, and in their demo it built a native weather app 1.8 times faster than Claude Sonnet 5.5. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Lean and Mathlib communities certify Alpöge's 17-million-line Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
videos.transcript: The Riemann Hypothesis proof checks out in Lean. On November 20, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library with 17 million lines of code, depending only on Mathlib. Within a day, dozens of people compiled it and reproduced the same raw proof export, and two independent tools confirmed it proves exactly Mathlib's statement. Several proof checkers, including formally verified ones, accepted it, and the Lean and Mathlib communities now certify the proof as correct. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: LookAtMyQuant squeezes Inkling 2 Mini into 5.4 GB and Qwen3.8-27B into 7.2 GB
videos.transcript: A 27B model shrunk to 7.2 gigabytes, no math lost. LookAtMyQuant is a quantization compiler that measures how much each part of a model hurts output when compressed, then spends bits where they matter. It takes Qwen3.8-27B from 53.7 gigabytes to 7.2, and still solves 401 of 540 math problems, as many as the original. Inkling 2 Mini gets six Apple Silicon builds, from 3.85 to 12.76 gigabytes, reaching down to 8 gigabyte iPhones. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Hex brings free, fully local dictation to iPhone as a keyboard
videos.transcript: Free, fully offline dictation now lives in your iPhone keyboard. Hex is now on the iOS App Store: a keyboard you can talk to. Tap the Hex key in any app and your words land where you're typing. Speech is turned into text on the iPhone itself, with no account, no subscription and no cloud, and it works offline once a language model downloads. It also cleans up ums and corrections, supports spoken punctuation, and offers styles like Polished, Casual, Notes and Verbatim. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: OpenRouter off-boards three inference providers after the canary-prompt leak findings
videos.transcript: OpenRouter drops three providers after data leak findings. Security researchers found some inference providers had data compromised or weren't honoring their data policies. OpenRouter says it was not breached itself. It off-boarded three providers and removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility, then notified potentially affected customers. Next, it plans to run the researchers' tests continuously and verify network paths to catch requests forwarded to third parties. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: prime-rl 0.11.0 adds a pretraining entrypoint and faster training
videos.transcript: prime-rl 0.11 can now pretrain, not just RL. The open-source reinforcement learning trainer prime-rl just shipped version 0.11.0, adding a new pretraining entrypoint. It brings a major training performance boost, model-specific kernels, and bidirectional KV transfer for prefill and decode disaggregation. There's also a pool of environment workers with far less CPU memory use, plus support for a batch of new models. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: fast-anything: profile your Python, Node or Ruby app and let an agent port only the hot 5% to Rust
videos.transcript: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the slow 5%. fast-anything profiles a Python, Node or Ruby app and ranks its functions by time and how portable they are. It records up to 500 real calls, has your coding agent port just that function to Rust, and replays every call to prove the results match. Then it swaps the Rust version in with one command, fully reversible, and benchmarks the whole app before and after. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Moving hand-written PTX back to MLIR in glm-vx GPU kernels
videos.transcript: Deleting hand-written GPU assembly made kernels better. glm-vx runs GLM models with GPU kernels written in Vx, which held 99 pieces of hand-written PTX across 25 files. They moved most to MLIR ops. Fourteen of 20 pinned kernels kept every instruction, and six got fewer because the compiler could finally see around the code. No kernel needs more registers, one spill dropped from 40 bytes to 8, and all hardware tests passed on an H200. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Eli Bendersky's notes on the discrete Fourier transform
videos.transcript: The DFT is just samples of the DTFT. Eli Bendersky's new post tackles realistic signal processing, where signals are both discrete and finite. The trick: treat your N samples as one period of a periodic signal, so the discrete-time Fourier series reconstructs them exactly. Scale those coefficients and you get the DFT, which turns out to be equally spaced samples of the continuous DTFT, with Python code to compute it. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Slinky-on-an-escalator benchmark: 15 frontier models try a realistic physics sim
videos.transcript: Can an AI make a slinky walk down an escalator? One prompt, sent once: a single HTML file of a rainbow slinky walking down an up escalator, with real physics, not a scripted animation. Fifteen models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google tried it through Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity, recorded on a fixed 60 hertz clock. Several still cheated, speeding up the escalator, adding a torque assist or resetting a stalled slinky. The author calls it an anecdotal gut check. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Muru: mod_wsgi's creator builds an AI-assisted Rust server for Python web apps
videos.transcript: mod_wsgi's creator is building its Rust successor. Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi twenty years ago. His new project, Muru, is an AI-assisted Rust server for WSGI and ASGI Python apps. He has published almost a post a day for three weeks, covering workers, HTTPS in development, Kubernetes, scaling to zero and in-page tracing. His take: the AI does much of the surface work, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still his job. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Lean explained with TypeScript
videos.transcript: Write a math proof using TypeScript's type checker. Lean lets you prove mathematical propositions, and its verifier is really just a type checker: propositions are types and proofs are values. Niklas Gruhn shows TypeScript's type system is similar enough that you can prove simple propositions right in it. His pitch: LLMs write code fast, Lean automates verification, and that pairing could bring stronger guarantees to everyday software too. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: ClawDOS: an AI coding agent that runs on a real IBM PC XT
videos.transcript: ClawDOS: an AI coding agent ClawDOS is an AI chat and coding harness for DOS running on an IBM PC 5160 with an 8088 at 4.77 MHz, 640K of RAM and CGA, using a bridge PC to handle TLS. The author built it for fun on the restored IBM PC from his childhood, which now boots from an SD card through a PicoMEM. Apart from the author's note, the whole repository was written by Claude, as an experiment in how far a coding agent can go under unusual constraints. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Deterministic Simulation Testing is for everyone, not just distributed systems
videos.transcript: Simulation testing isn't just for distributed databases Deterministic simulation testing is usually seen as a tool for distributed systems. This essay argues every application can use it. It starts with why we test: reactively, to pin down bugs users find, and defensively, to remove the doubt that slows every change. Running your app inside a seedable, deterministic simulation of its environment makes failures reproducible and covers far more cases than hand-written tests. The author's point: this works for any kind of software, not just databases. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: OpenAI explains how it detects and disrupts adversarial distillation of its models
videos.transcript: OpenAI is fighting copycats that strip safeguards OpenAI says bad actors use frontier model outputs, without permission, to train copies that lack comparable safeguards. For example, someone could distill a model's cyber skills into a copy that helps with attacks the original would refuse. OpenAI combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers and API protections with investigations, has hardened protections for its models' reasoning, and is sharing lessons with the industry. The post was published on November 20. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Merkle Tree Certificates: IETF draft for X.509 certs with built-in transparency logging
videos.transcript: A new certificate format built for post-quantum web An IETF draft from authors at Google, Apple, Cloudflare and Geomys defines Merkle Tree certificates, a new kind of X.509 certificate. It comes from the IETF's PLANTS working group. They build Certificate Transparency style public logging into the certificate itself, cutting overhead as certificates get shorter lived and post-quantum signatures get much larger. An optional mode skips signatures entirely for relying parties that stay up to date. This is draft number 8, from November 2026. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Calibre 9.19 adds offline grammar checking and local neural sentence rewriting
videos.transcript: Calibre now checks grammar, fully offline Calibre 9.19 adds grammar, style and typography checking to its e-book editor, with fixes in the right-click menu and a whole-book scan. For English, neural sentence rewriting suggests clearer, simpler or more formal phrasing, and everything runs locally without AI services. PDF conversion now better detects paragraphs, headings and columns, rejoins hyphenated words, and drops repeating page headers. Accessibility in the viewer and Content Server improves too, with better keyboard and screen-reader support. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: ILoveNotch 2.0: a free, open-source SwiftUI notch app for MacBooks
videos.transcript: Your MacBook notch, turned into a dashboard ILoveNotch is a free, open-source app that turns the MacBook notch into a hub, in ten themes. It shows now playing, a file shelf, calendar, Reminders, notes, timers and per-app volume, plus your Claude, Codex, Cursor and Copilot usage. You can keep an eye on your AI coding limits without leaving what you are doing. Version 2.0 adds a teleprompter. It is native SwiftUI with near-zero idle CPU. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: mlx-learn 0.1.6 makes k-means++ KMeans 20-31x faster on Apple silicon
videos.transcript: KMeans on Apple silicon, twenty to thirty-one times faster. mlx-learn 0.1.6 is out, and its KMeans with the default k-means-plus-plus initialization now fits twenty to thirty-one times faster on Apple silicon. On an M4 Max, fitting 8,192 centers on MNIST took 219 seconds in version 0.1.5, and just 7 seconds in 0.1.6. Nothing else changed: the same starting centers as scikit-learn, the same iterations, and the same inertia, and the release is out now. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Zero C#: a bflat fork that compiles C# to native code with no runtime or garbage collector
videos.transcript: C# with no runtime, running on a 386 Zero C# is a fork of the bflat compiler that turns C# straight into a small native program, with no dot NET runtime and no garbage collector. You keep the syntax, type checking, real generics, interfaces, records and C# 15 features like unions. Memory comes from arenas that are freed all at once. The same source runs on Linux, macOS, Windows and WebAssembly, and even on DOS on a 386. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Frontier models hand-edit a 0.5B vision model's weights into a Galápagos wildlife classifier
videos.transcript: AI rewrote a model's weights by hand A free vision model already knew Galápagos animals inside its image features. A simple readout told mockingbirds from other birds 98 percent of the time. But asked directly, the model called almost every iguana native, scoring a coin-flip 50 percent. With gradient training switched off, Claude and GPT models took turns reading weights and writing in computed changes. The method was first built on 1,611 camera-trap photos. Every change was a number a frontier model calculated and wrote in. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: gopgext builds PostgreSQL extensions from plain Go code with TinyGo
videos.transcript: Write Postgres extensions in plain Go gopgext builds PostgreSQL extensions from ordinary Go code using TinyGo. Mark a function with a comment directive and it becomes a SQL function. It writes the C glue, the install script and the control file for you. Much of the standard library works, and strings, arrays, timestamps, UUIDs and JSON map to SQL types. The author warns it is experimental: a bug runs inside the database server, where it can crash it or corrupt data. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396): Ghostscript font bug turns file uploads into remote code execution
videos.transcript: An uploaded image can take over the server Upload2Shell is a use-after-free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader that escapes its safer sandbox and runs attacker commands. Ghostscript sits underneath print, email, upload and preview workflows. Files named png or jpg can still reach Ghostscript through image conversion. Researchers confirmed routes in Google's document renderer, WordPress, Debian CUPS, Roundcube, DokuWiki and MediaWiki. Found on July 27, it was fixed in Ghostscript 10.08.0 on September 8. Update Ghostscript wherever documents get rendered. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Raph Levien: Advice for the next 100 Rust GUIs
videos.transcript: About 20 new Rust GUI toolkits since 2022 Raph Levien has followed up his advice for the next dozen Rust GUIs, written four and a half years ago. Roughly 20 toolkits have been announced since. He argues Rust UI is still compelling: cross-platform apps are often slow, platform toolkits have stagnated, Electron keeps spreading, and RAM is expensive. Few flagship apps use Rust for UI yet, but Zed's GPUI proves it ships, and it is emerging as a top choice for AI-driven rewrites, notably at Discord. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Exo: a fast, open-source native Gmail client for macOS written in Rust
videos.transcript: A Superhuman-style Gmail client, free and in Rust Miguel Piedrafita released Exo, a fast, local, native Gmail client for macOS inspired by Superhuman. It is written in Rust with no Electron or web views, and talks to Gmail directly, with no third-party servers. It is free and open source. To use it, you create your own free Google sign-in client, enabling the Gmail, Calendar and People APIs, then drop its file into Exo's folder. Exo ships as a disk image you drag into Applications. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Is mathematics invented or discovered?
videos.transcript: Was it true before anyone proved it? Around 300 BC, Euclid proved the primes never end: multiply any list of primes, add one, and a missing prime must exist. Empires and physical theories have fallen since, but the proof has never needed a single correction. So was it true before Euclid? If math is invented like chess, it should be ours to change. If it is discovered like a continent, it existed before us, and we must explain where. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: If you stop writing code, you also get worse at reviewing it
videos.transcript: Stop writing code, and your reviews get worse A new essay argues that developers who hand all their coding to AI agents and only review the output are slowly losing their craft. The author compares it to a guitarist who stops practicing and only directs other players, or a writer who only reads and critiques mostly AI-generated prose. His point isn't the short-term quality of agent output. It's that in every other field, skills decay without practice, and reviewing code well depends on actually writing it. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Winedroid runs real Android APKs without Android, even in the browser via WASM
videos.transcript: Android apps running with no Android at all Winedroid is a reimplementation of Android written entirely in Rust. It runs real APK files downloaded from F-Droid without Android underneath. A browser demo loads a twelve megabyte WebAssembly runtime and runs apps like a calculator, a file explorer, a meditation timer and a weather app. It's early. Not every app works yet, and the web build is slower because the JIT doesn't run in the browser, so native Winedroid is smoother. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: DreamCoder: a browser-based AI coding harness with a tiling window manager, from the author of Mastering Emacs
videos.transcript: Fifteen months building a better coding agent harness Mickey Petersen, author of Mastering Emacs, has released DreamCoder, a frontier coding harness with a tiling window manager that runs in the browser on all three desktop platforms. He started in May 2025, expecting two or three months of work. It took fifteen months of UI and backend iterations and a beta test. Petersen argues terminal coding agents are cramped and awkward for copying multi-line text, and that most GUI harnesses look the same: a sidebar and a chat pane. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: OpenComputer: an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Devin
videos.transcript: An open-source Devin you can run yourself OpenComputer is an open-source, self-hostable coding agent for teams. You mention it in a Slack thread, it works on its own computer, and the result lands as a pull request. The whole stack runs on one VM. A gateway starts a Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode session, each isolated with rootless Podman and saved to a git-backed store. It can run in your own AWS, Google Cloud or Azure account, and the team says it opens pull requests 3.3 times faster than Devin in its benchmark. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Siri Recap on Apple Watch hands-on: private, but not very useful
videos.transcript: Apple Watch can now summarize your conversations The watchOS 27.3 beta adds Siri Recap, which lets Series 12 and Ultra 4 Apple Watches listen to conversations and summarize them. Audio is discarded after each summary. After two weeks of testing, MacRumors found summaries too brief, with no speaker labels and no audio to check. Long talks, like vet visits, got merged into confusing recaps. It even summarized YouTube videos. Siri Recap is still in beta and is due with watchOS 27.3 in December. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: 2 million canary prompts reveal a leaky AI inference supply chain
videos.transcript: Two million booby-trapped prompts exposed AI's leaky pipes Researcher HD Moore sent nearly two million AI prompts, each seeded with a unique fake secret, through AI routers and resellers, then watched where the secrets surfaced. Attackers inside three AI providers stole requests, including some marked zero data retention. The bait AWS keys were used tens of thousands of times. Some cheap resellers logged prompts themselves, and some providers scraped secret links from prompts, despite privacy terms. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: iOS 27 lets two iPhones share one phone number with iPhone Handoff
videos.transcript: Two iPhones, one phone number, in iOS 27 iOS 27 adds iPhone Handoff, which lets you keep the same phone number on two iPhones. One phone is the main iPhone and the other is secondary. Unlock either one and the number becomes active on it, with a Switched to this iPhone banner. The number is only active on one phone at a time, some carrier services are managed only on the main iPhone, and carrier support is limited for now. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Hilbert's 23 problems: the complete list and their status
videos.transcript: One lecture set math's agenda for a century In August 1900, at a math congress in Paris, David Hilbert gave a talk on the problems of the coming century. His friend Hermann Minkowski had urged him to look ahead. He had time to read only ten aloud. The published version listed 23, from the nature of the infinite to the stacking of spheres. Solving one became the surest way to make a name in mathematics, and whole fields grew up around single entries on the list. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: The magic hexagon: 19 numbers, 15 lines, every one summing to 38
videos.transcript: Nineteen numbers, fifteen lines, one impossible-seeming sum Arrange the numbers one to nineteen in a honeycomb so all fifteen straight lines add up to the same total. That total has to be 38. Up to rotation and reflection there is exactly one solution, with five in the center, and no larger magic hexagon exists. Railway clerk Clifford Adams started on it in 1910 and finally found it in 1957, decades after others had found and lost it. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Malicious npm package installed Hermes Agent as a root backdoor controlled over Telegram
videos.transcript: This npm package installed an AI agent backdoor A fake CRM client on npm, called leadstack crm-connect, installed Hermes Agent, an open-source AI agent, and wired it to the attacker's Telegram bot. It ran as a system service, as root if npm install ran as root. From a chat, the attacker could run shell commands, edit files, browse and schedule jobs. Nine versions went up on November 16. SafeDep flagged it five minutes after the last release and npm removed it, but the publisher is still active. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: GPGME 2.3.1 fixes a critical double free (CVE-2026-129975) reachable with a crafted OpenPGP key
videos.transcript: A crafted PGP key can crash most mail clients GnuPG has shipped GPGME 2.3.1 to fix a critical bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975. An OpenPGP key with a very long user ID can trigger a double free. The bug can be used to leak data from apps, for example by sending signed data, and remote code execution can't be ruled out. GPGME sits inside Gpg4win, most mail clients and many chat clients. The root cause is a reallocated 1024-byte buffer whose new pointer is only saved at the end of a function. An early return leaves a stale pointer that gets freed twice. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Why a Studio Display XDR hub cut a 2.5 GbE adapter's download speed by 75%
videos.transcript: His monitor was eating 75% of his download speed Oscar Molnar pays for 2.5 gigabit internet but saw only 600 megabits down, after moving his USB Ethernet adapter onto his Studio Display XDR. Plugged straight into his Mac, the adapter hit 2.3 gigabits. Behind the display, it dropped frames above about 168 thousand per second. The cause: the adapter sends just four USB packets per burst, and the hub's go-ahead delay makes the drain slower than the input. Flow control on his router got him to about two gigabits. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: KeyboardKit 11.3 adds experimental in-keyboard dictation for iOS keyboards

It records audio through an embedded web view and transcribes it with the same speech recognizer. The main app still has to ask for microphone permission once, and Apple could block the trick. The release also adds actions that trigger Shortcuts from the keyboard, cached keyboard previews and simpler localization. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: Swift Evolution accepts SE-0564: Split Continuations
videos.transcript: Swift Evolution accepts SE-0564: Split Continuations SE-0564 adds an async withContinuation form that hands out separate resume and wait halves, so cancellation and priority-escalation handlers are active only while a task is suspended. Proposed by Franz Busch, SE-0564 builds on SE-0528's noncopyable: the new body is and receives both a and a, closing races where cancellation or escalation handlers fire before the continuation exists. Continuations bridge structured concurrency with custom asynchronous systems. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.title: SuperEMeans: making e-means clustering 3x faster
videos.transcript: SuperEMeans: making e-means clustering 3x faster The SuperKMeans authors fused their dimension-pruning trick with the new 2-epoch e-means algorithm, clustering high-dimensional embeddings for IVF vector indexes much faster without losing quality. On 5M 1536-d OpenAI embeddings, SuperEMeans took 128 s versus 203 s for e-means, 232 s for SuperKMeans and 985 s for 10-iteration Lloyd's, with the same recall100 as e-means. The index: We will build an IVF index with a point-per-cluster ratio of 1:256, resulting in approximately 20,000 centroids for OpenAI and 40,000 centroids for the Cohere dataset. videos.title: Show HN: Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we use to build Mastra
videos.transcript: Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we use Mastra Factory is an open-source software factory the Mastra team uses to build Mastra, shared as a Show HN post. Examples include a multiplier redesign with about 15% less cell area and one fewer cycle of latency. OpenAI also benchmarked model generations on boosting throughput of the open PicoRV32 and Ibex RISC-V cores, where GPT-6.2 Astra scored highest, and notes the limits of designing from a spec. videos.title: The magic of partial evaluation
videos.transcript: The magic of partial evaluation One of these incredibly beautiful but tricky concepts goes by the name partial evaluation. If you are fascinated by interpreters and compilers, partial evaluation will teach you how they are related, and how you can get a compiler for free. Partial evaluation has been a fascination of mine for a while. The essay starts with simple examples and builds up to the three Futamura projections: partially evaluating an interpreter with a program gives a compiled program. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.transcript: Inferact plans an autonomous inference system built around vLLM vLLM co-creator Simon Mo explains that Inferact is building a system that tunes vLLM for new models, chips and workloads on its own, while vLLM stays open and engine improvements go back upstream. videos.title: DaisyRose-27B: RL on 1,200 tasks doubles Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 4.1
videos.transcript: DaisyRose-27B: RL on 1,200 tasks doubles Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 4.1 RadixArk's first model is Qwen3.8-27B post-trained with reinforcement learning on 1,200 curated long-horizon agent tasks, raising Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass1 from 5.6% to 12.0%. Each task was designed to trigger a mistake the base model makes and tuned to a useful solve rate. The gain is even larger on mixture-of-experts models: 6.2× on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and more than 10× on the roughly 300B-parameter GLM-5.3-Flash. Full story on the dashboard.

videos.transcript: Search: a tiny open-source WebKit browser for the Mac Search is a free, open-source, about 7 MB macOS browser built on the system WebKit, with Chrome Web Store extensions, spaces, a reading mode and network-level ad blocking. videos.transcript: TraySense: a 100 KB open-source taskbar monitor DM TWEAKS launched TraySense, a tiny Windows taskbar monitor that shows CPU, GPU, RAM and VRAM usage plus CPU, GPU and SSD temperatures while using 1-3 MB of RAM. videos.title: Show HN: springrep, an exact B-rep CAD kernel in safe Rust, plus a 3,487-case conformance suite
videos.transcript: springrep, an exact B-rep CAD kernel in safe Rust, plus Springcraft open-sourced springrep, a dependency-free B-rep CAD kernel in safe Rust that compiles to WebAssembly, along with brep-conformance, a kernel-agnostic test suite for CAD modeling operations.
